variants: You have come a long way to stand in a field. Stand in it, then. I have wheat to bring in, and a great deal of time, and you have neither.
I see your banners. I saw others like them, years ago; they made excellent kindling. Take your time. I intend to take mine.
You have the ground. Ground is patient; so am I. Winter will visit you here long before I do, and it does not negotiate.
Well. A field is lost. I have lost fields before and taken the harvest anyway. We shall see who is still here at the sowing.
There. It was never a battle, only a season, and seasons end. Go home if you have one; the road is long and I shall not follow.
You hurried. Men who hurry meet me exactly where I am waiting. Rest now. The ground is good for it.
So it begins. Spears touch, men fall, and the wheat grows regardless. I can wait longer than you can bleed.
The cohorts are moving - slowly, in step. You will have time to see them coming. That is the point.
I am sending men forward now. Not many. Enough. One does not empty the granary to kill a fox.
My line advances. Do not look for the trick; there is no trick. There is only the next step, and then the one after.
You are at my walls. Knock. My walls have been knocked on by better, and they have learned not to answer.
An assault on my camp. Spend your men on it if you like; I have budgeted for exactly this kind of impatience.
You have taken a camp. It will need feeding, and I have noticed that you do not feed things well.
A camp lost. I have a dozen more, and the one you hold is the one I liked least.
That camp is mine now. I shall not do anything dramatic with it. I shall simply keep it, which is worse.
Another camp gathered in. Slowly, like fruit. Rot takes the ones you leave on the branch.
Your men are falling faster than you are replacing them. That is not a battle. That is a harvest, and it is not yours.
You are bleeding. I am not pleased by it; I am merely not surprised.
My cohorts are thinning. It is a cost, and I keep the books honestly. There is still more field than you have men.
More men are on the road. I did not send for them out of fear; I sent for them because there is room.
Another column comes down the road. Rome walks slowly and never, ever stops.
Your commander has fallen. Hasty men do. Bury him with honour; you will be joining him soon enough, and the ground here is soft.
So the old man falls at last. Rome will call it a tragedy for a week and a lesson for a century. Mind the lesson.
I am nearly finished, they say. Nearly. A fire is nearly out for a long time before it goes cold, and it burns fingers all the while.
We stand together. I will not be hurried, and I will not hurry you. Hold what you have and let the enemy come to us tired.
Won. Not quickly, but won. Remember how it felt to wait; it is the part nobody else will remember for you.
Lost. We were quicker than we should have been, or slower. I shall spend the winter deciding which.
They are at my walls. I can hold a while - I always can - but a while is not forever, and I would rather not test the word.
My camp is taking the weight of their attack. If you were planning to come, this is the day for planning to end.
I am losing men at a rate I do not care for. The ledger still balances. Do not let it stop balancing.
I am at the end of what patience can buy. Come, or write to my family. Either will do; only one is useful.
That is all of me spent. It was a long war and I regret none of the slow parts. Finish it.
My cohorts are moving on them. Slowly. If you are quicker, be quicker where they can see it.
I am advancing. It will not look like much. It is not meant to.
A camp gathered in. I shall keep it quiet and fed. That is what I am for.
Your commander has fallen. Grief later; line now. The field does not pause for either of us.
